Title: Stupid Outlook Express (not so much about VTES)

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
So I'm monkying around with outlook suck-spress as a newsreader, trying to
read this here newsgroup, and I can't for the life of me figure out how to
delete all the old messages. No matter what I do, all the messages stay
around, which is really irritating. Using Newswatcher (one might ask "if you
have used Newswathcer, why aren't you doing so now?", the answer being
something involving my wife and I having 2 different ISPs on the same
computer, and the Newswatcher is all configured for her ISP and she wants to
keep it that way, so I can't use Newswatcher, as she honeied it first, and
while I could probably set up a second set of configurations, if the Outlook
I'm currently using for e-mail, instead of Eudora for very similar reasons,
was convinient for reading newsgroups, that'd be all cool and stuff) , you
can look at a newsgroup, mark them all read, and then they all disapear, so
the next time you sign on, you only have the fresh new messages to look at
and read, and you aren't encumbered by the old, previously read messages.

Is there a way to make them all go away? Am I just stoopid?

Thanks,

Messages.Body:

Try Tools->Message Rules->News and create a rule that deletes all messages
that were send more than X days ago. There might even be a rule that deletes
all messages marked as read. I'm not sure how well it'll work because I keep
all of mine ( saves me having to search Google when I want to look up
stuff ).

Messages.Author: Santiago
Messages.Body:
In article <B8E4F2CB.13D%PD...@bigplanet.com>,
Peter D Bakija <PD...@bigplanet.com> wrote:

>Using Newswatcher (one might ask "if you have used Newswatcher, why

>aren't you doing so now?", the answer being something involving my
>wife and I having 2 different ISPs on the same computer, and the
>Newswatcher is all configured for her ISP and she wants to keep it
>that way, so I can't use Newswatcher, as she honeied it first,

With Newswatcher, you can create as many servers as you want via
the News Servers command in the Special menu. Each is independent of
the other. Each file of newsgroups that you store keeps track of what
server the groups are on, so your wife and you can each have separate
files with your groups in them, and no one is bothered by the other.
(If you're using plain old Newswatcher instead of MT-Newswatcher, you
should switch. It's still free, but substantially more full-featured.)
